head: 476a817c96a6
answers: The reviewer's round-2 changes request at c7010979: both important findings and all six minor ones, none deferred. Eight threads answered and resolved.

proof.criterion: Important 1: the document-wide `ambiguous` says something false whenever no placement was kept - a selection across a block break, or a held send written before the placement field existed
proof.surface: Dispatch's web app in Chromium through Playwright, against the real Go server and PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector, and the proof-editor and margin unit suites
proof.command: cd packages/dispatch && bun run e2e -- compose-wait
proof.observed: 12 passed (6.1m). A sixth refusal reason, `unremembered`, answers the document-wide step when no placement was kept, with its own sentence: 'The words you selected read in more than one place, and nothing kept of where you selected them says which one this <kind> is about. Your draft is kept - select the text again to attach it.' `ambiguous` keeps its wording and now means only readings whose surroundings really match - the block step, and the document step when a placement was kept. The cross-block row asserts that exact sentence and that neither 'no longer where you selected it' nor 'with the same text around them' appears. The three null-placement unit rows moved to the new reason, each comment naming the case it drives; the real-placement row keeps `ambiguous`. The false comments the reviewer named are corrected, including 'none of the four' where there are six.
proof.negativeControl: The cross-block row's two new assertions are the control: at c7010979 the composer showed the 'same text around them' sentence for a case where the text around the two readings differs, and that row's text check now refuses it.

proof.criterion: Important 2: a jj conflict marker from the forward merge is in the published API reference, and its ANCHOR_MISSING entry breaks the one-sentence-per-line rule
proof.surface: The repository's own line-break check and the file
proof.observed: Exit 0 (it was 1 at c7010979, R1 at 2430). The marker line is gone - `grep -n '>>>>>>>'` finds nothing in the file - and the entry is three sentences on three lines. Its third sentence now states the rule the sweep implements: the mark is kept while its author has a browser on the room, and its minute runs from the moment that user's last browser left.
proof.negativeControl: The check exits 1 on the entry as it stood, which is how the reviewer found it; the file now passes the same command.

proof.criterion: The six minor findings, and nothing else in the application broken by them
proof.surface: The whole Chromium e2e project, and both unit suites
proof.observed: 938 passed, 0 failed (1.0h) - including e2e/hover-preview.e2e.ts:87, which failed on this pod in earlier rounds and on main, so the two-core timing it depends on went its way this time. The six: held-sends' comment is true of the composer's own Retry and `retry()` returns void; `registerComposer` has its own context so no composer re-renders on margin hover, selection or placement; the pending report carries whether its count covered every row this tab had written and the waiter answers only such a report; one `textOf(block)` backs all three block-text reads; the re-anchor waits, bounded, for the reader's own document to bind rather than saying it is not open; and index.html is byte-identical to main again.
proof.negativeControl: `git diff origin/main -- packages/dispatch/web/index.html` is empty, which is the whole claim for that one; `bunx biome check packages/dispatch` is clean with main's version, so lint never required the re-indentation.

filesChanged: packages/proof-editor/src/record-mark-retype.ts and tests/record-mark-retype.test.ts (the sixth reason, the corrected comments, one textOf)
packages/dispatch/web/src/features/margin/margin-context.tsx, margin-context.test.ts, MentionComposer.margin.test.tsx (the new sentence, the composer registry context, the bridge-bind wait)
packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/README.md (the marker and the line breaks), packages/dispatch/web/index.html (reverted to main)
packages/dispatch/e2e/compose-wait.e2e.ts (my own row 12 only: the exact sentence asserted)
trickyParts: Closing the pending-count race needed `pending-sync.ts`, outside the files the finding named: the waiter sees only `PendingState`, and whether a count ran before or after a row's write is known only where the count is taken. The report carries it as optional fields, so no other reader of that state changed.

`ambiguous` and `unremembered` are different claims about the same shape of failure: the first says the surroundings match in more than one place, which is only knowable with a placement; the second says nothing kept says which reading was the reader's, which is the honest thing to say when nothing was kept.
openQuestions: The reported 'about ten seconds' is still unexplained, as every round has recorded.
discoveredComplexity: The pod was restarted mid-round and the commit was unpushed. The INFRA merge lane saved it as legion/INFRA-727-rescue; I continued on it rather than redoing it, and deleted the rescue branch. The commit id is unchanged, which matters because the eight resolved review threads each cite it. Work in progress now goes to legion/INFRA-727-wip, which starts no pull-request CI.

No forward merge this round: GitHub reports the pull request MERGEABLE (mergeStateStatus BLOCKED is the required reviews and checks, not a conflict), and the branch already carries main's two CI fixes, #2551 and #2552.
e2e/hover-preview.e2e.ts:87 passed this time, after failing on this pod in rounds 3 and 5 and on main as well. It is timing, not this change, and the record now has it both ways on the same branch.
The simplify pass is spent (round 1, ce-simplify-code at 96a647eb, applied). A round answering a review runs none.
